scDifformer architecture and tissue distribution of the training dataset. ( A ) Overview of the three-stage training framework of scDifformer, including pre-training, post-training, and fine-tuning. The model introduces a diffusion-based post-training stage following conventional MLM pre-training to refine transformer representations. This stage integrates the advantages of both transformer and diffusion models, enhancing knowledge acquisition and accelerating convergence. ( B ) Tissue composition of the scRNA-seq dataset used for pre- and post-training, comprising over 34 million cells across diverse human tissues.

Benchmarking cell annotation performance in intra- and inter-dataset setting. ( A, B ) Box plots showing the accuracy of eight cell annotation methods across five scRNA-seq datasets in intra-dataset (A) and inter-dataset (B) settings. For intra-dataset evaluation, five-fold cross-validation was performed within each dataset. For inter-dataset evaluation, each dataset pair was used once for training and once for testing. ( C ) Confusion matrices for kidney sample annotations in the inter-dataset setting, comparing scDifformer, Geneformer, and scBERT.

Attention-based identification of cell-type-relevant genes and functional enrichment. ( A ) Heatmaps showing log-transformed attention weights from the final transformer layer of scDifformer. The top 10 genes with the highest attention scores are shown for B cells, ciliated cells, fibroblasts, and natural killer (NK) cells from the Travaglini lung dataset. Colored columns represent the attention maps for each cell type: light blue for B cells, ochre for ciliated cells, dark blue for fibroblasts, and red for NK cells. ( B ) Bar plots of -log 10 P -values from cell-type enrichment analysis using the top 100 attention-weighted genes for each cell type. Most significantly enriched term in each case matches the true annotated identity. ( C - F ) GO enrichment of top 100 genes with the highest attention weights in each cell type (C: B cells; D: ciliated cells; E: fibroblasts; F: NK cells). Each node represents one enriched GO term; node color groups similar functional categories, node size reflects the proportion of input genes mapped to the term, and edge width indicates semantic similarity between terms.

Comparison of scDifformer and the other models embeddings for immune cell resolution and developmental trajectory inference. ( A ) UMAP projection of unintegrated single-cell gene expression profiles, colored by cell type (top) and tissue of origin (bottom). The embedding shows pronounced batch effects and poor separation among cell types. ( B ) UMAP and Slingshot-inferred pseudotime trajectories based on scVI embeddings. While scVI reduces batch effects, the resulting trajectories are sparse and exhibit limited biological directionality. ( C ) UMAP and pseudotime trajectories derived from scDifformer embeddings. Cells of the same type form compact, continuous clusters with clear lineage transitions from HSPCs to differentiated immune subsets across bone marrow, spleen, thymus, and peripheral blood. Compared to scVI, scDifformer better preserves developmental continuity and aligns more closely with canonical hematopoietic hierarchies. ( D ) UMAP and Slingshot-inferred pseudotime trajectories based on scFoundation embeddings. ( E ) UMAP and Slingshot-inferred pseudotime trajectories based on scGPT embeddings.

scDifformer in spatial transcriptome deconvolution. ( A ) Schematic overview of scDifformer-GraphSAGE for deconvolution of spatial transcriptomics data. We first randomly generated the pseudo-ST data with cell mixtures from scRNA-seq data. Based on the pseudo- and real-spots, we find the k -nearest neighbors for each spot using the expression matrix and construct a link graph containing all the spots. Based on the link graph, the graph convolutional network is utilized to propagate both pseudo- and real-spots data into the latent layer and discern the compositions of distinct cell types in each spot. The cell embeddings extracted from scDiffomer will be concatenated with the spot expression matrix as the input of GraphSAGE module. Finally, we get the spot-cell-type matrix containing the proportion of each cell type in each spot. ( B ) A spatially resolved single-cell transcriptome dataset from mouse cortex. Each dot represents a single cell, and colors represent different cell types. We grided these cells based on their coordinates to generate spots with known cell type composition. ( C, D ) Radar charts showing the ranking of deconvolution performance of different methods measured by PCC, SSIM, RMSE, and JSD. The outermost layer of a radar chart represents the best performance, including the highest PCC/SSIM and the lowest JSD/RMSE. Gridded spots of single-cell level mouse cortex sample (C) and simulated spatial transcriptome data from scRNA-seq of Human pancreas data (D) are used as test samples.
